{"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"---"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE :-
1) TO BE CASE HARDENED UPTO 55~60 HRC.
2) CASE DEPTH 0.8~1.2mm.
3) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT.
4) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"The title-block heat_treatment field is '---' while note N2 specifies case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a case depth of 0.8–1.2 mm and that threads are to be kept soft, but neither the title block nor the note states at which manufacturing stage the heat treatment applies (e.g., before or after final machining). This ambiguity can cause the supplier to apply the treatment at the wrong point in the process, resulting in distorted features or incorrect hardness. The designer should update the heat_treatment field and note N2 to explicitly state the manufacturing stage for the case hardening.","recommended_correction":"Update the title-block heat_treatment field and note N2 to specify the exact manufacturing stage at which case hardening is to be performed (for example, 'after rough machining, before finish grinding')."}]}
